content.value_statement: App interaction tasks require reliable targeting and visible verification across device interfaces. This skill guides agent-device commands for navigation, inspection, verification, and session cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Guides opening an app in the foreground and reading the initial interactive snapshot.
Describes pressing, clicking, filling, long-pressing, scrolling, and returning with settled UI updates.
Uses printed UI differences and named expectations to guide interaction verification.
Explains scrolling to a selector or to the end of content.
Preserves exact reference tokens and prioritizes references and selectors over coordinates.
Guides screenshot-based targeting when accessibility information is unavailable, with topic-specific help for specialized tasks.
limitations: The reviewed skill contains instructions only; it requires an available agent-device CLI and a configured target environment.
Screenshots and platform-specific actions depend on support provided by the external tool.
Sparse or unavailable accessibility data requires image inspection and coordinate targeting.
The file does not include executable tests, installation instructions, or detailed specialized command references.

use_cases.title: Verify a Mobile App Flow
use_cases.description: Navigate a test app, interact with current UI references, and verify an expected screen before closing the session.

use_cases.title: Reproduce an Interface Issue
use_cases.description: Repeat authorized navigation steps and inspect snapshots or supported screenshots to document the observed interface state.

use_cases.title: Plan a TV App Check
use_cases.description: Consult topic-specific help for TV controls, then plan app navigation and a named verification step on a configured target.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [test app] with agent-device on the configured target. Summarize its initial interactive snapshot, then close the session.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the initial app state.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [test app], navigate to [screen] using current references, verify [expected text], then close the session.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Off-Screen Target
prompt_templates.prompt: In [test app], scroll until [selector] is visible, interact with it, and verify [expected state]. Preserve exact references and close the session.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: locate a target in scrollable content.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Sparse Accessibility Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [test app] on my configured test target. If accessibility data is unavailable, inspect a screenshot and use coordinates only as needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: recover UI targeting when references are unavailable.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: open a configured test app and summarize its initial screen.
output: Illustrative result: the app opened in the foreground and returned an interactive snapshot.
The visible screen contained a title and selectable controls with reference tokens.
The session was closed after inspection.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: find an off-screen settings entry and verify the destination.
output: Illustrative result: scrolling to the selected entry made it visible.
Selecting the current reference opened the destination screen.
The expected heading was verified, and the session was closed.

best_practices: Use authorized test targets and confirm the app scope before interacting with sensitive or consequential controls.
Copy reference tokens exactly, including suffixes, and prefer current references or selectors over coordinates.
Verify a named expectation after actions and close the session when the workflow finishes.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse references from sparse or unavailable accessibility snapshots.
Do not repeat bare scrolling when a selector-based scroll can locate the target.
Do not treat interface changes as proof of success without checking the expected result.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Execution still requires the agent-device CLI and a configured target.

faq.question: Which platforms does the skill describe?
faq.answer: It describes iOS, tvOS, macOS, Android, and Amazon Vega OS TV apps in Vega Virtual Devices.

faq.question: Does the skill install agent-device?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed file provides workflow guidance and does not include installation instructions or a bundled CLI implementation.

faq.question: How are interface targets selected?
faq.answer: The guidance prefers current reference tokens, then ID, label, or role selectors. Coordinates are a last resort.

faq.question: What happens when accessibility data is unavailable?
faq.answer: The guidance recommends inspecting a screenshot, using coordinates, and retrying an interactive snapshot after navigation.

faq.question: How does the workflow verify completion?
faq.answer: It checks a named expectation through wait, is, get, or find commands, then closes the agent-device session.
